tools.description: Read canonical source text by one LID or an inclusive LID range. Use when: Read source text after a LID has been located. Do not use for lexical discovery when no LID is known.  Returns data.text with at most 8,000 Unicode characters per page, data.source_range for this page and data.requested_range for the requested LIDs. Ranges are absolute canonical-source UTF-16 [start, end), not byte offsets. Preserve the publication and range when continuing. Copy published_book_ref from book_list and check its available_tools. Costs 1 call on success, including empty results, each continuation page and repeated successful requests; failures cost 0. complete=false means more pages exist; copy needed next_calls name and arguments unchanged. sources gives published_book_ref, start_lid/end_lid, source_range and source_url: cite only evidence actually read, retaining its version and exact range. An empty sources array provides no source citation. usage is the server's post-call balance with charged_units and charged_from; do not infer balance locally. On quota_exhausted stop content retries and report usage.free_resets_at plus top_up_url or top_up_instruction; book_list and mcp_usage remain free.

Returns usage: free_remaining, paid_remaining, free_resets_at (next Hong Kong month), paid_next_expires_at and call_packs with per-batch expiry and available_units. If both balances are zero, stop content retries and tell the user the reset time and top_up_url, or top_up_instruction when the URL is null. The user arranges purchase; a purchase does not grant material access. No evidence sources or continuation pages are returned.
